ceo_directive_recall: #2 should continue in parallel, but do not let it become an endless simulation refinement branch.
crux_question_single_sentence: Does the multi-mechanism architecture (size-selective filter + hydrodynamic retention) achieve the pre-registered buyer threshold of ≥30% therapeutic retention at 90 days AND ≥85% drainage preservation, for ALL THREE payload classes (antibody 150 kDa, peptide 5 kDa, small molecule 500 Da), ROBUSTLY across patient variability (CSF production rate ±2×, degradation rate ±2×)?

crux_question_decomposed.Q_A_threshold_achievement: For each payload class (antibody, peptide, small_molecule), does multi-mechanism achieve (a) retention_90day ≥ 0.30 AND (b) drainage_preserved ≥ 85%?
crux_question_decomposed.Q_B_pareto_optimality: For each payload class, is multi-mechanism Pareto-optimal (i.e., NOT dominated by any single mechanism — size_sel alone, hydrodynamic alone, or mechanical_valve alone)?
crux_question_decomposed.Q_C_robustness: Does the threshold achievement hold at the WORST-CASE patient variability (90th percentile), not just the nominal case?
crux_question_decomposed.Q_D_selectivity: Does the architecture actually achieve SELECTIVE retention (drug retained while CSF water drains) — or is the apparent retention just slower drainage that retains everything proportionally (which is NOT selective and provides no therapeutic advantage)?

why_this_is_the_crux.rationale: The V18/V21 work claims multi-mechanism is the strongest architecture for payload diversity. The V21 verdict 'pareto=true for all payloads' is what supports continuing #2 as a SURVIVOR. If the crux question's answer is YES (multi achieves threshold for all payloads, robustly, and is Pareto-optimal), then #2 is a SURVIVOR. If NO, then #2 is either a NEGATIVE_CEILING (no architecture can do it) or an ARCHITECTURE_CHANGE (multi fails but a different mechanism could succeed).
why_this_is_the_crux.what_one_question_determines_verdict: Does multi-mechanism Pareto-dominate hydrodynamic alone for peptide and small_molecule payloads? V18 data shows hydrodynamic alone achieves 0.484 retention at 92% drainage for peptide/small_molecule, while multi achieves 0.376 retention at 90% drainage. Hydrodynamic alone STRICTLY DOMINATES multi for these payloads. If this holds under patient variability, multi-mechanism is INFLATED and #2 must be adjudicated NEGATIVE_CEILING or ARCHITECTURE_CHANGE.

T1_retention_90day.target: >=0.30 (30% of initial therapeutic concentration retained at 90 days)
T1_retention_90day.applies_to: ALL payload classes (antibody, peptide, small_molecule) — must hold for ALL, not just one
T1_retention_90day.rationale: 30% retention at 90 days corresponds to ~2.5x increase over no-shunt baseline washout (which yields ~12% at 90 days per WASHOUT_MODEL.json). Below 20% retention, the washout problem is not materially solved.

T2_drainage_preserved.failure: <0.80 (less than 80% drainage — risk of ICP elevation per FOULING_ICP_SIMULATION.json which shows 50% fouling = 50% drainage drop = 6 mmHg pressure = HIGH ICP risk)
T2_drainage_preserved.rationale: Hydrocephalus drainage is the primary indication for eShunt. If retention mechanism reduces drainage below 85%, the patient is at ICP risk. 85% is the lowest defensible clinical minimum.

T3_robustness_90th_percentile.target: Retention at 90th-percentile worst-case patient variability >=0.20 for ALL payload classes
patient_variability_axes: CSF production rate: 0.5x to 2x nominal (21 mL/hr) — clinical range per WASHOUT_MODEL.json
Degradation rate (membrane fouling / hydrodynamic resistance increase): 0.5x to 2x nominal — clinical range per FOULING_ICP_SIMULATION.json (50% fouling at 90d is realistic)
Protein concentration in CSF: 0.5x to 2x nominal (affects fouling rate)
T3_robustness_90th_percentile.rationale: Patient variability is wide. A mechanism that works only at nominal conditions is not clinically viable.

T4_selectivity.target: Multi-mechanism achieves retention ratio (drug_retention / water_retention) > 1.5 for at least 2 of 3 payload classes
T4_selectivity.failure: Ratio <= 1.2 — mechanism is just slowing drainage non-selectively
T4_selectivity.rationale: 'SELECTIVE retention' means drug is retained more than water. If a mechanism slows drainage for everything proportionally (e.g., hydrodynamic alone), it is NOT selective — it just reduces drainage.

T5_pareto_optimality.target: Multi-mechanism is Pareto-optimal (not dominated by any single mechanism) for ALL 3 payload classes
T5_pareto_optimality.failure: Multi is dominated by any single mechanism for ANY payload class
T5_pareto_optimality.rationale: If multi is dominated by a single mechanism for any payload class, then the added complexity (size-selective filter + hydrodynamic in series) is not justified — the simpler single mechanism is strictly better. This is the anti-inflation check on V21's 'pareto=true' verdict.

verdict_rule_pre_registered.SURVIVOR: All 5 thresholds (T1-T5) PASS for ALL 3 payload classes → multi-mechanism is the load-bearing invention.
verdict_rule_pre_registered.NEGATIVE_CEILING: T1 or T2 FAILS for any payload class AND no alternative single mechanism achieves both thresholds → architecture cannot solve the problem; freeze with documented negative ceiling.
verdict_rule_pre_registered.ARCHITECTURE_CHANGE: Multi fails T5 (Pareto) for some payload classes but a DIFFERENT mechanism (e.g., A2 affinity-based, A3 reversible flow interruption) could plausibly achieve both thresholds → identify new mechanism, authorize V-next.
verdict_rule_pre_registered.NOT_READY: Critical question cannot be answered without in-vitro data (e.g., actual membrane retention efficiencies are unknown to ±30pp) → identify specific milestone required.

anti_inflation_commitments: Threshold declared BEFORE Step 3 simulation (this file is timestamped before T2_CRUX_SIMULATION.json).
T1-T5 must hold for ALL 3 payload classes, not aggregate.
T4 selectivity check explicitly distinguishes 'selective' from 'slower drainage'.
T5 Pareto check uses PROPER pairwise domination (multi must not be dominated by ANY single mechanism for ANY payload class).
Worst-case (90th percentile) — not nominal — must satisfy T1-T2.
NO use of 'LIKELY_NOVEL' or 'pareto=true' without numeric domination proof.

minimal_simulation_required_to_answer_cr.scope: Re-run V18 retention model with PROPER Pareto comparison + patient variability sweep + 180-day durability check.
minimal_simulation_required_to_answer_cr.what_is_minimal: Single Python script, <300 lines, runtime <60 seconds. Reuses V18's first-order washout model (no new physics). Adds: (1) explicit Pareto domination check per payload class, (2) 9-point patient variability grid per payload class (3 axes × 3 levels = 9 cases, take 90th percentile worst), (3) 30/90/180-day durability.
minimal_simulation_required_to_answer_cr.what_is_excluded: No CFD. No finite element analysis. No multi-physics coupling. No in-vitro correlation. No Monte Carlo over continuous parameter space (just 9-point grid).
minimal_simulation_required_to_answer_cr.expected_outcome_per_V18_data: Multi-mechanism will PASS T1 (retention >=0.30) for all payloads at nominal. Multi will PASS T2 (drainage >=85%) for all payloads. Multi will FAIL T5 (Pareto) for peptide and small_molecule because hydrodynamic alone (0.484, 92%) dominates multi (0.376, 90%). Verdict will likely be NEGATIVE_CEILING for multi-mechanism, with size-selective alone as a partial SURVIVOR for large payloads (antibody only).

what_would_change_my_verdict.if_V18_numbers_are_wrong: If a corrected simulation shows multi achieves >=0.50 retention for peptide/small_molecule at >=90% drainage (i.e., the V18 multi retention calculation is too conservative), the verdict could flip to SURVIVOR.
what_would_change_my_verdict.if_pareto_definition_differs: If buyer accepts 'Pareto-optimal for at least one payload class' rather than 'for ALL payload classes', then multi could survive as the antibody-specific architecture. But CEO directive 'do not let #2 become endless refinement' suggests we should not narrow the claim post-hoc to antibody-only.
what_would_change_my_verdict.if_hydrodynamic_is_prior_art: If hydrodynamic retention alone is fully disclosed in prior art (e.g., generic flow-restriction valve), then hydrodynamic cannot be patented alone and multi-mechanism is the only novel combination — even if dominated by hydrodynamic alone, multi could be SURVIVOR if the buyer accepts 'slightly worse performance but patentable'. This is a patent-vs-engineering tradeoff that should be escalated to counsel.
